sections.h2: How can a Jacksonville homeowner sell fast?
sections.html:
Your choices are a listing with an agent, a cash offer, or a sale to an as-is purchaser who takes on the repair bill and the house untouched. Whichever you choose, two witnesses sign the deed and the Duval County clerk records it. How quickly it all happens depends on the buyer's financing, the state of title and any lien that needs a payoff letter.

The city is huge and varied, which means the best route changes house by house. A well-kept house in a sought-after neighborhood can do well on the open market. One that needs a roof, rewiring or storm repair, or is tangled up in tenants or an estate, often fits a cash or as-is buyer, since no lender inspection stands in the way.

  • Listing: biggest buyer pool, longest timeline, lender appraisal and repair requests.
  • Cash or as-is: fewer conditions, and you price the condition in.
  • Family transfer: still a conveyance for value, and the homestead rules below still apply.

Jacksonville merged with Duval County in 1968, and it bills itself as the largest city by area in the continental United States, covering 747.29 land square miles. Population is estimated at 1,017,689 for July 2025. One municipal government covers beach communities, a riverfront downtown, suburban subdivisions and rural edges, so conditions differ block by block and a neighbor's experience may not match yours.

A typical owner-occupied house is worth $293,700, owners live in 57.6 percent of homes, and the middle rent is $1,465. Because permit, utility and code questions all go to one city, a single call there tells you about open permits before you list.

sections.h2: How Duval's homestead exemption plays into a sale
sections.html:
Selling ends your exemption, and the buyer files a new one. In Duval the base amount is $25,000, with up to $25,000 more on value above $50,000, and that second layer does not reduce school taxes.

After a sale the assessed figure jumps to market value on the next tax roll, and the Save Our Homes ceiling of 3 percent or less on yearly increases starts over for the new owner. A buyer who held a Florida homestead in any of the three prior roll years can file for portability, a separate application. The timely date for both is March 1, and late filing runs to early September.

Duval renews exemptions automatically each January 1 when nothing has changed, and a renewal card arrives as a receipt. The office also has a brochure on how short-term renting can affect exemptions, which landlords should read before listing a house they once lived in. For forms, call 904-255-5900 or email pacustserv@coj.net. Visit 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260.

sections.h2: Other exemptions a buyer or seller might mention
sections.html:
Beyond the basic homestead, the Duval appraiser runs many other exemption categories, and a buyer's eligibility for one can affect an offer. Before closing, ask the office whether a given benefit carries over or has to be refiled.

  • Military and service members: armed forces deployment, disabled veteran, and service-connected total and permanent disability exemptions.
  • First responders: a total and permanent disability exemption for them and their surviving spouses, and a homestead exemption for surviving spouses of military personnel or first responders.
  • Seniors: a senior citizen exemption with its own application and the Duval 501 form.
  • Other: blindness, widow or widower, disability, a granny-flat assessment reduction for parents' or grandparents' quarters, conservation land, and institutional or non-profit exemptions.
  • Historic preservation: available through the City of Jacksonville.

Several forms are handed out by phone or email, so call 904-255-5900 to make sure you hold the current version.

sections.h2: Where the sale proceeds from here
sections.html:
Two offices will carry most of your questions. The Duval County Property Appraiser covers exemptions and portability, and the Duval tax collector quotes the balance due. The city itself handles permits, utilities and code questions, so one call there can show whether any work on the house is still open.

Next, decide how you want to sell. A tidy house in a sought-after area may net more through an agent, though showings and a lender's appraisal slow the schedule. A house with a worn roof, tenants or a tangled estate often moves quicker to a buyer who pays cash and accepts it as is. Whatever the route, collect offers in writing, compare the amount you keep rather than the headline price, and confirm who pays recording and deed tax before you sign. Keep the lease, tax bill and permit receipts in one folder so a buyer can verify the house quickly.

Here the deed rate matches the rest of the state, 70 cents for each $100 paid, and every signer is liable. A mortgage on the property is part of the consideration, assumed by the buyer or not.

You pay the clerk at the recording counter. Section 28.24 fees open at $5.00 for a first page and rise with extra pages, names and technology charges.

Property tax has its own rhythm: January 1 sets value, November brings bills, early-payment discounts shrink through February, and April 1 marks delinquency. At closing the title agent prorates the year, so get your actual balance from the Duval tax collector rather than guessing.

sections.h2: Foreclosure, an estate or a tenant
sections.html:
• Foreclosure: once final judgment is entered, the clerk schedules a public sale 20 to 35 days later, unless the lender agrees to a longer gap. Homestead owners should check with the clerk within 10 days after the sale about leftover funds.
  • Estate: summary administration fits a modest estate, meaning $150,000 or under outside exempt assets, or a death over two years ago.
  • Tenants: someone renting by the month must get 30 days' notice. A tenant who raises any defense other than payment has to deposit accrued rent with the court within five days of service.

sections.h2: What to prepare before a Jacksonville buyer visits
sections.html:
• Recorded deed, survey if you have one, and the latest tax bill.
  • Payoff letters, and association paperwork for condos and HOAs.
  • Receipts and permits for the roof, major systems and storm repairs.
  • Lease copies and rent ledgers if the house is occupied.
  • For an inherited home, the court order authorizing the sale.

With a signed contract, the title agent runs the title search, gathers payoff letters, drafts the deed and arranges the two witnesses. The clerk then records the deed and collects the tax. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, though you should ask for a written timeline from any buyer.

faqs.q: Does Jacksonville charge a different deed tax?
faqs.a: No. Duval uses the usual 70 cents per $100, and only Miami-Dade stands apart.

faqs.q: When is the Duval homestead deadline?
faqs.a: March 1 every year. A late filing is accepted until early September, which is 25 days after proposed-tax notices go out in mid-August.

faqs.q: Does a buyer inherit my homestead benefit?
faqs.a: No. The sale resets value to market for the next roll, and the buyer applies for a new exemption.

faqs.q: Can I sell with a tenant living there?
faqs.a: Yes, and the buyer should get a copy of the lease. A tenancy by the month ends on 30 days' notice. Unpaid rent starts with a three-day written notice.
